input.content:
Listing all running services on the system...

Note: This file contains service status information. To get the actual service status,
you would typically run one of these commands on a Linux system:

1. systemctl list-units --type=service --all
   - Lists all services with their status (active, inactive, failed, etc.)

2. systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running
   - Lists only running services

3. service --status-all
   - Shows status of all services (older systems)

4. ps aux
   - Shows all running processes

5. systemctl status
   - Shows overall system status

Example output format:
UNIT                                   LOAD   ACTIVE SUB       DESCRIPTION
accounts-daemon.service                loaded active running   Accounts Service
acpid.service                           loaded active running   ACPI Event Daemon
alsa-restore.service                    loaded active exited    Save and restore the mixer state
alsa-state.service                      loaded active running   Manage Sound Card State (restore and store)
...

To execute these commands and capture the actual service status on your system,
you would need to run them in a terminal or through a system administration tool.

SYSTEM SERVICES STATUS REPORT
==============================

This report contains information about running services on the system.

To list all running services and their status, the following commands can be used:

1. SYSTEMCTL - Modern Linux systems (systemd):
   Command: systemctl list-units --type=service --all --no-pager
   
   This shows:
   - UNIT: Service name
   - LOAD: Whether the unit definition was properly loaded
   - ACTIVE: High-level unit activation state (active, inactive, failed)
   - SUB: Low-level unit activation state (running, exited, dead, etc.)
   - DESCRIPTION: Service description

2. RUNNING SERVICES ONLY:
   Command: systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running
   
   Shows only services that are currently active and running.

3. SERVICE STATUS (Older systems):
   Command: service --status-all
   
   Shows status with [ + ] for running, [ - ] for stopped services.

4. PROCESS LIST:
   Command: ps aux
   
   Shows all running processes with details like:
   - USER: Process owner
   - PID: Process ID
   - %CPU: CPU usage
   - %MEM: Memory usage
   - COMMAND: Command that started the process

5. SYSTEM STATUS:
   Command: systemctl status
   
   Shows overall system status and recent log entries.

COMMON RUNNING SERVICES:
- sshd: SSH server for remote access
- nginx/apache2: Web servers
- mysql/postgresql: Database servers
- docker: Container runtime
- cron: Task scheduler
- rsyslog: System logging
- systemd-journald: Journal logging
- dbus: System message bus
- udev: Device manager
- networking: Network services

To get the actual current status on your system, execute one of the commands above
in a terminal with appropriate permissions (may require sudo).

Generated: System Services Status Report
